$meta.name: TaskPriority
$meta.description: Priority tier of a maintenance task or service request.
$meta.ownerNote: Canonical is what MOBILE already speaks (`taskPriority*`); the admin panel speaks a short form. Same inversion as VendorTradeType, milder: the installed binary sends the long form, so the long form wins.
$meta.onUnknownNote: Unlike the trade list this vocabulary is CLOSED — four tiers, no more. The API normalizes then pipes through a Zod enum, so an unrecognized priority is a 400, not a passthrough.
$meta.aliasMatchNote: The API lowercases and trims before the alias lookup, so `LOW`, `Low` and `low` all resolve. Only the distinct real-world spellings are listed.

provenance.aliasesFrom: task-priority.ts:26-37 (PRIORITY_ALIASES) plus mobile's legacy `taskPriorityUrgent` alias (babel_localized_enums.dart:465-472). The API's lowercased-canonical entries (`taskprioritylow` …) are an artifact of that case-insensitive lookup, not distinct wire spellings, so they are not listed.

drift.note: Two vocabularies for four values, and THE TOP TIER HAS TWO NAMES — the kind of disagreement a shared file exists to end.
drift.admin: 4 SHORT forms — `low` | `medium` | `high` | `urgent` (src/lib/tasks/priority.ts:19-28), re-declared inline a second time in operations/tasks/new/tasks-form-schema.ts:136-141
drift.topTier: Canonical is CRITICAL. `urgent` is the admin panel's short form for it — not a fifth tier, and not a different severity.
drift.column: tasks.priority is a plain STRING (Task.ts:163) — no DB constraint holds this.
